While it is certain that S.’s ideas for PU must have originated before this date, it is equally
plain that S.’s specific conception of the first three acts owes a great deal to the Shelleys’
journey through the wintry Alps in March 1818, and their rapid transition to a warm Italian
spring. This experience seems to have prompted a coalescence in S.’s imagination of many
diverse literary, philosophical, political, scientific and personal influences, to produce a poem
which, in the scale and quality of its achievement, goes far beyond anything S. had hitherto
written. His thinking towards the project matured through the first Italian summer of 1818,
as he busied himself with translations of Plato’s Symposium, Euripides’ Cyclops (see Longman
ii 371–412, no. 172), various other classical translations, and much other reading connected
